subject: Game Theory
title: Multihoming and Switching Costs
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Multihoming and Switching Costs.

hook.text: You use both Uber and Lyft—comparing prices before each ride. That's multihoming.

buildup.text: When users can easily use competing platforms, no platform achieves winner-take-all dominance.

discovery.text: Platforms fight multihoming with loyalty programs, exclusive content, and data lock-in.

twist.text: High switching costs on one side can coexist with low costs on the other—creating asymmetric competition.

climax.text: The EU's Digital Markets Act forces interoperability, lowering switching costs to break platform dominance.

punchline.text: Lock-in is the platform's real product.
